8.1 Automated decision-making

Automated decision-making takes place when an electronic system uses personal information to make a decision without human intervention. We are allowed to use automated decision-making where HMRC has a lawful basis under our statutory powers. This includes where it is necessary and proportionate for the purposes of the assessment and collection of taxes or duties or determining benefits and credits. For instance, in some circumstances HMRC uses automated processing to generate penalties and changes to notices of coding.

If you are subject to an automated decision, we have appropriate measures in place to safeguard your rights. You will be notified in writing at the time, including the reasons for the decision and any associated consequences. You will have 30 days to request a reconsideration or a new decision not based solely on automated processing. Where appropriate you should provide additional information relevant to your circumstances and HMRC will inform you in writing of the reviewed decision.

If we make an automated decision based on any particularly sensitive personal information:

we must have your explicit written consent

it must be necessary for the performance of a contract, or justified in the public interest

We must also put in place appropriate measures to safeguard your rights.

8.2 What we need from you

As part of our security measures, we sometimes need to ask for specific personal information from you to help us confirm your identity and validate your right to access the information, or to exercise any of your rights.

You can continue to contact HMRC to change your address and personal details, or for other purposes relating to your specific concerns. You can also contact the Valuation Office.

9. Contact HMRC or make a complaint

9.1 Data protection Officer

HMRC has appointed Data Protection Officer (DPO), to oversee compliance with its data protection obligations.

You can find information about how to contact the DPO in section 9.2 of this notice.

9.2 Complain to HMRC

If you want to complain about how HMRC has handled your personal information, you should follow the HMRC complaint process.

You need to state the business area relating to your complaint. The complaint will enter a process for formal consideration and assessment.

If you think that the data protection matters have not been fully resolved by HMRC’s complaints process, email HMRC’s Data Protection Officer to review your concerns: advice.dpa@hmrc.gov.uk.

You can also use one of the postal addresses to make a complaint about HMRC, and mark it for the attention of the Data Protection Officer.

If you’re not happy with HMRC’s resolution to the complaint you can submit your complaint to the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO), the UK supervisory authority for data protection issues.

You can contact the Information Commissioner on the Information Commissioner’s website, which has more information about data protection and your rights.

If you have any questions about this Privacy Notice or how HMRC handles your personal information, email the Data Protection Officer at: advice.dpa@hmrc.gov.uk.

10. Changes to the Privacy Notice

We keep our Privacy Notices under regular review. If there are any changes we will explain what has been updated on the HMRC Privacy Notice front page, for example, any new uses of personal data.

From time to time, we may also tell you in other ways about the processing of your personal data.

11. List of HMRC supplementary Privacy Notices

Notice title and link Description

Automatic Exchange of Information Privacy Notice This Privacy Notice explains how HMRC collects and uses the personal data it receives from UK financial institutions and overseas tax authorities in relation to Automatic Exchange of Information agreements.

Childcare Service Privacy Notice The HMRC Childcare Service is an online platform provided by HMRC that allows eligible parents and guardians in the UK to apply for and manage government childcare support schemes.

Data sharing with the Office for National Statistics This Privacy Notice explains how HMRC shares personal data with the Office for National Statistics (ONS) and how they use the data.

Government Gateway Privacy Notice The Government Gateway is a secure online identity verification and authentication system administered by HMRC to access a wide range of government services. It acts as a central login platform for both individuals and businesses, enabling them to interact with various government departments through a single account.

Help to save Privacy Notice The HMRC administered Help to Save scheme is a government-backed savings account designed to support people on low incomes by rewarding them for saving. `

HMRC app Privacy Notice This Privacy Notice explains how HMRC and other organisations may use your data when you use the HMRC App.

HMRC Developer Hub Privacy Policy The HMRC Developer Hub is an online platform provided by HMRC that enables software developers to integrate their applications with HMRC’s digital services. This privacy policy relates to the information we store about Developer Hub user. It does not relate to the privacy of the end users of any applications under development.

Open Banking Privacy Notice HMRC Open Banking is a modern, secure payment method that allows individuals and businesses to pay their taxes directly from their bank accounts using Open Banking technology. This Privacy Notice describes how HMRC uses your personal information when you use Open Banking to make a payment.

We’ll therefore use your personal information for any of the purposes set out if we reasonably consider that we need to do so.

2.4 Artificial Intelligence and machine learning

HMRC uses Artificial Intelligence (AI) and machine learning techniques where the law allows us to support the department’s strategic objectives, including for the:

assessment and collection of taxes and duties

prevention or detection of crime

AI helps us:

learn more about large amounts of data

improves our service delivery

prevents and responds to customer error and non-compliance

Where the use of AI could impact customer outcomes, HMRC makes sure that:

the results are explainable

there is an option for human involvement

the results are contestable

we are compliant with our data protection, security, and ethical standards

We are also exploring new possibilities to test fast-evolving technologies in areas where it has not yet been used, while at the same time assessing and managing the associated risks.

Your individual rights also apply to HMRCs use of AI. You will be provided context specific information if we use AI to make an automated decision about you, including how to request a human review. For more information read the sections in this Privacy Notice about ‘Data Protection information rights’ and ‘automated decision making’.

3. The kind of information we hold about you

Personal data, or personal information, means any information about an individual from which that person can be identified directly or indirectly. It does not include data where the identity has been removed (anonymous data).

We process data about:

members of the public

customers and clients

businesses, including their employees

suppliers and service providers

advisers, consultants and other professional experts

complainants and enquirers

agents and representatives

relatives, children, guardians, dependants and associates

offenders and suspected offenders

employees and prospective employees

We collect, store and use certain categories of personal information about you such as:

contact details such as name, title, addresses, telephone numbers, and personal email addresses

sex and gender

marital status and dependents

National Insurance number

bank account details

information about your income

information about your employment

information about your business activities

information about your domestic and business properties

passport and driving licence information

We’ll also collect, store and use certain information, which is more sensitive personal data, when it is relevant to our functions, including those defined by the UK GDPR as special category data, such as:

biometric data, such as voice recognition data for identity verification

information about criminal convictions, allegations and offences, where relevant in relation to our functions

health data where it is relevant to claims for Tax Credits or Universal Credits

health data where it is relevant to our commitment in the HMRC Charter to give you extra support if you need it

Special Category Data requires a higher level of protection.

Read the HMRC appropriate policy document to find out how HMRC processes particularly sensitive personal information.

3.1 Transaction monitoring and cookies

In order to protect your data and our services HMRC operates transaction monitoring capabilities. This records how you connect to our systems, and what you do whilst you are on them. Read more information in our transaction monitoring Privacy Notice.

Read about cookies on GOV.UK and cookie settings on HMRC services.

4. How your personal information is collected

We collect personal information directly from you in circumstances such as:

when you submit your Income Tax and other tax returns — this could also be received online or from third parties, including third party software

when you register with HMRC for VAT or other purposes

when you claim tax credits or Child Benefit

when you register for one of HMRC’s services

when we enable you to access HMRC and other government services

when you contact Valuation Office about rating lists, valuation lists and valuation of property

when you contact Rent Officers for the provision of valuations and other advice for Housing Benefit and fair rents

when you apply for Tax-Free Childcare

when you call the HMRC helpline, and we routinely record calls for our functions and for quality, training and security purposes

whenever you contact us

when you apply for a job at HMRC

We’ll also collect your personal information directly from third parties such as:

your employer when they provide us with your information for Income Tax and National Insurance purposes

other government departments and public authorities

credit reference agencies

banks and other financial institutions

publicly available sources

other people you do business with, for example, digital platforms

your agent or representative

overseas tax authorities

previous employers and referees

landlords and letting agencies

4.1 If you fail to provide personal information

If you fail to provide certain information when legally required to do so, you may be subject to penalties. We’ll tell you when you are legally obliged to provide information and the consequences of not doing so.

4.2 Your responsibility to inform us of changes

It is important that the personal information we hold about you is accurate and current. You need to keep us informed if your personal contact information changes.

5. Data sharing

We will, in some circumstances and where the law allows, share your data with third parties, including:

third-party service providers — read ‘Section 2.1’

other government departments and other bodies

public authorities and law enforcement agencies, both in the UK and overseas

EU institutions
